### Observed differences

- The execution order between the activities A19, A20 and A25 on one side and A26, A27 and A28 on the other reversed. In the earlier window, A19, A20 and A25 ran before A26, A27 and A28 in nearly every trace where they co-occurred (A19 preceded A26 in about 36 of 100 traces and followed it in almost none; A25 preceded A27 in about 38 of 100). In the later window the picture is mirrored: A26 and A27 now precede A19, A20 and A25 (A26 before A19 in about 31 of 100 traces, A19 before A26 in almost none; A27 before A25 in about 29 of 100). [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL006, REL007]

- In the later window, A19, A20 and A25 sit much later in the trace: their mean position moved from about one-third of the trace (0.33, 0.33, 0.32) to about three-fifths (0.59, 0.61, 0.60), while A26 (0.35 to 0.33) and A27 (0.58 to 0.56) barely moved. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]

- Successions changed accordingly. Earlier, A19, A20 and A25 led almost exclusively to A26 (about 92, 94 and 99 of 100 observed outgoing transitions); in the later window they lead mainly to A28 and A32 (A19 about 48 and 45; A20 about 43 and 56; A25 about 39 and 56). A27, which earlier led almost only to A28 (about 98 of 100), now also feeds A19, A20 and A25 (about 42 of 100 combined); A28, which earlier led almost only to A32 (about 99 of 100), now also feeds them (about 43 of 100 combined). A45, which earlier fed A25, A19 and A20 (roughly 35, 35 and 24 of 100), now leads to A26 in about 94 of 100 transitions. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006]

- Close successions moved with the block: A45→A25 and A19→A26, previously adjacent in about 93–94 of 100 cases, are nearly unobserved in the later window (1–2 supporting observations); A45→A26 became adjacent (gap 1 in about 94 of 100, previously a 2-step gap); A27→A19, A28→A19 and A28→A20 became close successions (from 1–2 observations earlier to 32–75 later); and the gap A27→A32 stretched from two steps (about 97 of 100) to three steps (about 93 of 100). [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG010, LAG011]

- Participation is essentially stable, so this is a reordering of existing behaviour rather than activities appearing or disappearing: A19, A20 and A25 occur in roughly a quarter to two-fifths of traces in both windows (for example A19 in 75 of 200 earlier and 66 of 200 later), and A26, A27 and A28 in essentially all traces in both windows. In the later window the order between A20/A25 and A28 is mixed (A28 before A20 in about 21 of 100 traces, A20 before A28 in about 17), whereas earlier A20 and A25 consistently preceded A28. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, DIR005, REL005, REL008]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the block of activities A19, A20 and A25 was repositioned: in the earlier window it ran between A45 and A26 (before A27 and A28), while in the later window A45 leads to A26, and A19, A20 and A25 run after A26 and A27, interleaved with A28 and before A32. The order flip is shown directly by the relational items for all pairs between the two groups; the position shift affects exactly A19, A20 and A25 while A26 and A27 stay in place; the successor and adjacency changes point the same way; and participation of every involved activity is stable, so this is a reordering rather than activities being added, removed or made optional. The volume of evidence also far exceeds what an unchanged process produces: 30 items qualified where about 0.4 would be expected by chance, and each item's difference is larger than in about 199 of 200 random re-splits [screening, DIR001, POS001, REL001, LAG001]. Limitations: positions and gaps are measured in event order, not clock time, so this is an ordering change and not evidence about timing; several items describe the same underlying rearrangement and are not independent confirmations; and the new order between A19/A20/A25 and A28 is mixed, so the exact new arrangement is only partially determined. A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is a shift in the mix of two trace variants (one with the block early, one with it late) rather than a single repositioned block, since the comparison is at window level. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, POS001, POS002, POS003, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, LAG001, LAG003, LAG007, LAG008, LAG011]

Other differences: none that stand apart from the rearrangement above; the slight position advances of A26 and A27 and the wider A27→A32 gap fit the relocated block now sitting between A27 and A32. [POS004, POS005, LAG006]
